findings.claim: The source-3 precedence assertions are real in a bare shell but silently disappear whenever the ambient environment carries an absolute GIT_INDEX_FILE — which is exactly what `git commit` sets when committing from a linked worktree or with `-a`, i.e. inside this repo's own pre-commit eval gate — so the git-first mutation the acceptance names goes GREEN precisely where the gate is enforced, and nothing is reported.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:876-892 `_temp_repo` runs `git commit --allow-empty` with `env=clean_full` (:995-997), which strips only GIT_LOCATION_VARS and GIT_SHA; an inherited absolute GIT_INDEX_FILE points the commit at another repo's index, the commit fails, `_temp_repo` returns None, and :1000 `if head:` skips all three precedence assertions with no `bad.append` — the resolution's claim that they 'skip loudly' (tasks/reviews/pr31-r1-resolution.json, R4 note) is false, the skip is silent and the case reports 0 failures either way. Measured hook environments: plain `git commit` -> GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/index (relative, harmless); `git commit -a` -> /tmp/r10b/.git/index.lock (absolute); commit from a linked worktree -> /private/tmp/r10b/.git/worktrees/r10b-wt/index (absolute). This PR was authored in a linked worktree.
findings.repro: GIT_INDEX_FILE=<an absolute path to another repo's index> python3 -c "...; print(ea._temp_repo(tempfile.mkdtemp(), clean_full)); <apply M6 git-first>; print(ea.check_build_identity(case))" -> None, then [] (M6 green). Without GIT_INDEX_FILE the same M6 gives 2 failures.
findings.acceptance: `_temp_repo` builds its checkout in an environment it controls (strip GIT_INDEX_FILE and the other per-invocation GIT_* vars, or pass `-c` overrides), so a repo is built under a pre-commit/worktree environment too; and if it still cannot, the skip appends a failure or is otherwise visible in the case output rather than silently reducing the assertion count. Falsifier: the M6 git-first mutation must be red with an absolute GIT_INDEX_FILE exported.

findings.claim: The repair makes `build-identity` go RED on a correct implementation whenever an ambient GIT_DIR is set: the local-dev assertion's oracle still measures HEAD with the unscrubbed ambient environment while the resolver now scrubs, so the two disagree — a false failure in exactly the pre-commit-hook condition this case's own history cites.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:1021-1027 computes `head` via `subprocess.run(['git','rev-parse','--short','HEAD'], cwd=ROOT)` with full env inheritance, then compares it to `build_id.git_sha(ROOT, dict(os.environ, GIT_SHA=''))`, which now strips GIT_DIR. With GIT_DIR pointing at any other repository, `head` is the stranger's sha and the resolver correctly returns this repo's. Before the repair both sides inherited GIT_DIR and agreed, so this is newly broken by the repair.
findings.repro: GIT_DIR=/tmp/r10/outer/.git python3 -c "...; print(ea.check_build_identity(case))" -> ["a checkout with a .git must report its own short sha '097e8b5', got '537dfdb'"]
findings.acceptance: The local-dev oracle measures HEAD in the same environment the resolver resolves in (strip GIT_LOCATION_VARS from the oracle subprocess too), so `check_build_identity` returns 0 failures with an arbitrary GIT_DIR exported, while M8 (dropping the resolver's scrub) stays red.

findings.claim: The repair updated the ADR and prompts for R2/R3 but left the eval case's own `triage` block stale: three of its six published mutation counts are now wrong, and its narrative still describes the half-fix R2 rejected as the fix.
findings.evidence: evals/adversarial/build-identity.json:19 `refalsified` publishes 'SHA_RE relaxed to `.+` (10)', 'precedence flipped so GIT_SHA outranks the build (1)', 'build_sha ignoring the file entirely (6)'. Re-measured on the repaired tree: 20, 2, 7 respectively (the resolution artifact itself records 20/2/7 for M4/M7/M9). :18 `red_first` still closes with 'Fixed in both — the resolver runs git in the environment it was handed', which is precisely the description ADR-027 §e and prompts/013 were corrected to retract ('The first fix was half of one'). This is the same class as R3 — published numbers/claims contradicting the artifact — inside the file that IS the spec.
findings.repro: Rebind build_id.SHA_RE to `.+` then ea.check_build_identity(case) -> 20 (case says 10); build_sha -> None -> 7 (case says 6).
findings.acceptance: `triage.refalsified` lists the mutation set and counts actually run against the repaired tree (the resolution's 10 mutations, or the six with corrected counts), and `triage.red_first` describes the scrub-in-`_rev_parse` fix rather than the environ-threading half.

findings.claim: The generalisation ADR-027 §g just retracted for R9 survives verbatim in the case file's `what_this_cannot_prove`, so the eval set still publishes 'the failure mode if any of that is false is the honest one and not a regression'.
findings.evidence: evals/adversarial/build-identity.json:17: 'The failure mode if any of that is false is the honest one and not a regression: BUILD_SHA is absent or empty, the resolver rejects it, and /api/meta reports `unknown` exactly as it does today.' ADR-027 §g now states the opposite for build-cache staleness ('no validation can detect it') and for build-abort. The case file is a document of record under CLAUDE.md's 'the eval set IS the spec'.
findings.acceptance: `what_this_cannot_prove` names build-cache staleness as the assumption that does not fail closed, matching ADR-027 §g.

findings.claim: Two of the three per-variable location-var assertions cannot fail: with a non-repository cwd, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_COMMON_DIR alone never make `git rev-parse` answer, so only GIT_DIR binds the scrub the code and prose describe as covering all three.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:973-981 loops over GIT_LOCATION_VARS; control measurement with the scrub removed and cwd a temp dir: GIT_DIR -> rc 0, '537dfdb'; GIT_WORK_TREE -> rc 128 'not a git repository'; GIT_COMMON_DIR -> rc 128. Mutation M8b (`_rev_parse` strips GIT_DIR only, keeps GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_COMMON_DIR) -> check_build_identity returns 0 failures, versus 2 for the full-scrub-removal M8.
findings.repro: Rebind build_id._rev_parse to a version whose env filter excludes only 'GIT_DIR', then ea.check_build_identity(case) -> [] (green).
findings.acceptance: Either the two extra assertions run in a state where those variables can actually redirect the answer (e.g. a real checkout as `root` with GIT_COMMON_DIR pointed at another repo), or the comment at build_id.py:31-36 and the case docstring stop claiming all three are held by a check.
